sources.entry: Claude Code Agents by Paul - UndeadList - Comprehensive E2E development workflow with helpful Claude Code subagent prompts for solo devs. Run multiple auditors in parallel, automate fix cycles with micro-checkpoint protocols, and do browser-based QA. Includes strict protocols to prevent AI going rogue.

summary.one_liner: A Claude Code plugin and per-project kit of 24 subagent prompts and 6 workflow skills for solo developers building Next.js/React/TypeScript apps, covering audits, fix cycles, browser QA, and deploy checks.
summary.what_it_does: The repo provides 24 agent definitions in an agents/ folder, including 11 audit agents (code quality, bugs, security, docs, infra, UI, database, performance, dependencies, SEO, API testing) meant to run in parallel, plus fix-planner, code-fixer, test-runner and test-writer agents. It also includes browser agents that use Chrome integration for UI navigation, console monitoring and screenshot comparison, deploy and environment validators, and an architect-reviewer supervisor. Six slash-command skills (/full-audit, /pre-commit, /pre-deploy, /new-feature, /bug-fix, /release-prep) chain these agents into workflows, with reports written to .claude/audits/. The README also documents protocols for limiting AI agents to approved, one-at-a-time changes with checkpoints and revert commands.
use_cases: Run parallel code, security, and performance audits before launch
Pre-commit and pre-deploy checks for a Next.js app
Automated find-fix-verify loop using browser QA
Generating a prioritized FIXES.md from audit findings
Writing failing tests before a bug fix or new feature
Drafting PR descriptions and seed test data
how_to_run: npx claude-code-agents (per-project install, run from project directory, Node.js >= 14)
notable: Audit agents are designed to run in parallel and write separate reports (AUDIT_CODE.md, AUDIT_SECURITY_DEEP.md, etc.) that fix-planner consolidates into FIXES.md
Explicit anti-rogue protocols: no unapproved changes, no package installs without approval, micro-checkpoints, and enforcement phrases
Browser QA agents use Chrome integration to find console errors and UI bugs in a loop
Installable as a Claude Code plugin or copied per project via npx or curl scripts
caveats: Tuned for Next.js/React/TypeScript with Prisma, npm/pnpm and Vercel; other stacks require editing the agent prompts
Skills such as /full-audit only work when installed as a plugin; per-project installs require natural-language prompts instead
Browser QA depends on Claude Code's Chrome integration being enabled
